chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
In a will that a woman witnessed, the testimony of a woman is valid for one-quarter of the will.
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of a woman's testimony in witnessing a will according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific application of female testimony in inheritance law, establishing that a single woman's witness is sufficient for one-quarter of the estate. This ruling is derived from the Quranic principle of two women equating to one man in financial matters, applied here to the validity of the will's execution rather than the total division. It highlights the Shia juristic approach to balancing evidentiary standards with practical estate distribution.
